messages:
sam: ran a targeted nsys sweep on a ded pool node (A100-80GB, driver 525). seeing repeating HBM bandwidth ramps that line up with KV page read spikes. long sequences (>=8192) show a big regression vs baseline — latency +12% p50 and large oscillations in per-kernel time. attaching quick summary and timeline snippet. :thinking:

aline: can you paste the exact nsys invocation and the timeline window you inspected? curious if the kernel-selector is flipping kernels mid-request.

sam: sure — command and the summary snippet below. i clipped the timeline 280–420ms where the pattern repeats.

```bash
nsys profile -o kvprobe --sample=cpu,gpu --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --capture-range=cudaApiTracing --duration=10s 
  --stats=true ./bin/kvserver --workload=longseq --seqlen=8192 --batch=3
```

nsys summary (selected):
- GPU HBM read peak: 780 GB/s (sustained bursts ~420–620 GB/s)
- Kernel timeline: attention_large_window_kernel / kv_prefetch_device alternating with small-window kernels at ~50–120ms intervals
- Significant DMA stalls aligning with large kv_read_system calls (kv page read bursts)

jordyn: that alternating pattern looks like kernel-selector handoff. recall we have a commit that widened the seqlen threshold from 4096->6144 for large-window kernels. maybe for 8k with certain batch shapes the selector oscillates because of per-batch token distribution.

pat: ran a quick microbench to reproduce locally (cpu-local, same model shaper):

```text
cmd: ./tools/kvmicro --seqlen 8192 --batch 3 --runs 50
avg latency: 128.3 ms (baseline 114.6 ms)
throughput: 23.4 toks/ms down from 26.1
evictions/sec: 1344 (vs baseline 820)
HBM peak read measured (perf): 640 GB/s during evict waves
```

pat: evictions/sec is huge — suggests prefetch / kvpager is thrashing pages instead of amortizing reads.

sam: hypothesis: our prefetch stride and the prefetch window are not aligned to page/kv-block boundaries for long sequences, causing cross-page DMAs and partial-page eviction. that plus kernel-selector jitter triggers heavy HBM read storms.

aline: fully agree. also suspect batching heuristics: we currently allow large sequences to be coalesced into single large-kernel launches when batch token variance is high. coalescing seems beneficial usually but here it amplifies contiguous KV access pressure.

jordyn: quick experiment idea: two-pronged approach
1) adjust prefetch: align prefetch to 2MB slab boundaries and increase prefetch_distance to 32 tokens for large seqs. throttle concurrent prefetch streams to 4.
2) change batcher: if seqlen > 4096, split into two micro-batches (chunking) so kernel-selector consistently picks low-BW kernels and KV reads are staggered.

sam: i ran a short A/B with the prefetch alignment tweak only (patched kvpager to align reads) — latency dropped ~6% and evictions/sec down 28% on the same microbench. not perfect but promising.

pat: i'm about to run the chunked-batcher experiment with a feature flag. will post numbers in an hour. plan: compare (a) current, (b) prefetch-align, (c) chunked-batcher, (d) both.

pat: quick note — to force the kernel-selector into the low-bandwidth kernels you can set the runtime flag: 
`--kernel_selector.prefer_low_bw=1` for testing. do NOT ship this flag globally yet.

dev-bot: created issue INF-4822: "kvpager longseq HBM thrash + kernel-selector oscillation" and linked this thread. :white_check_mark:

sam: summary / next steps:
- pat will run full A/B and attach perfetto/nsys traces for each variant (expected by EOD). :chart_with_upwards_trend:
- if chunked-batcher + prefetch-align shows >=8% latency improvement and evictions reduce >=30%, we'll ship a canary to dedicated pool and monitor HBM bandwidth traces.
- jordyn to bisect the kernel-selector threshold commit (starting point abc123) to see if the widening caused instability.
- aline to draft a small perf test for CI that exercises seqlen 8192+ with the kvpager metrics exposed.

sam: thanks everyone — tagging @aline @jordyn @pat for follow-ups.
